# Kip

> Kip is a plain-PHP, batteries-included framework for server-rendered apps:
> zero runtime dependencies, zero JavaScript, SQLite by default, PHP 8.3+.
> Routing, sessions, auth, migrations, caching, uploads, email, the audit
> log, and a schema-driven admin panel are included and tested. Kip runs
> unchanged on ordinary shared hosting and on the cheapest VPS tier, with no
> build step and no config wrangling.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what Kip is, the deployment contract, install paths.
- [Tutorial](docs/tutorial.md): build a working blog in about an hour.
- [User guide](docs/guide/README.md): the reference manual, sixteen
  example-first chapters.

## Reference

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): request lifecycle, cache
  invalidation, security lanes.
- [Design decisions](docs/design-decisions.md): what Kip will never include
  and why.
- [Versioning](docs/versioning.md): the stability and upgrade contract.

## For coding agents

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the repo contract agents should follow: hard
  constraints, commands, writing style, and the one-query performance budget.
- [Building with AI agents](docs/guide/16-building-with-ai.md): a
  tool-agnostic workflow for building Kip apps with AI agents, and how to
  add AI features to a Kip app without dependencies.
